descriptionChirho: The one true God, YHWH, the God of Israel — the dominant sense of Elohim throughout the Hebrew Bible, used with the article, in construct chains, with pronominal suffixes and prepositions, always referring to the covenant God.

Foreign or pagan gods in the plural — the deities of the surrounding nations, as in 'the gods of Egypt' or 'you shall have no other gods'; identified by Arabic آلِهَة, Korean 신들, Swahili miungu, Hindi देवताओं, Spanish dioses.

A single foreign deity — 'the god of Ekron' (2 Ki 1:2), 'Ashtoreth the goddess of the Sidonians' (1 Ki 11:5, 33), or 'their god' referring to a specific pagan deity; identified by Arabic إِلٰه/إِلَهَة (singular), Korean 신, Spanish dios/diosa, Hindi देवता.

A supernatural or godlike being — used of spirits, angels, or humans in a divine capacity, as in 'you shall be as elohim' (Gen 3:5) or 'I saw an elohim coming up from the earth' (1 Sam 28:13); identified by lowercase English 'as elohim', Hindi देवता, Korean 신 으로.
